title: Irish Bread
tagline: Graham flour, buttermilk, an X on top. No yeast, no waiting.
description: A family-card Irish soda bread made with graham flour and buttermilk: mix, knead briefly on a floured cloth, cut an X and bake 45 minutes. One round loaf, no yeast.
ingredients: 1 cup white flour, plus a lot more for the cloth
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a round baking pan.
Thoroughly mix the graham flour, white flour, baking soda and salt.
Add the buttermilk and mix until all the batter is wet.
Flour a pastry cloth with a lot of flour. Turn the dough onto it and sprinkle more flour over the top. Knead just until it holds together, then place it in the pan.
Cut an X on top with a knife.
Bake 45 minutes, until browned and the bottom sounds hollow when tapped.
notes: The dough is wet and sticky. That's why the card says a lot of flour on the cloth. Use it, and knead only a few turns.
Graham flour is coarse whole-wheat flour. Plain whole-wheat flour works if you can't find it.
Soda bread starts rising the moment the buttermilk hits the soda. Get it in the oven right away.
Best the day it's made. Toast it after that.
troubleshooting: Dense, tough loaf → kneaded too long; a few turns only.
Flat and spread out → dough too wet for the pan, or sat too long before baking; flour the outside well and bake immediately.
Soapy or metallic taste → soda not mixed through; whisk the dry ingredients thoroughly first.
source: Adapted from a family recipe card
